claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I have one child, Alex, who is 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 10 years old.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means either you live with Alex, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me, but I do help out with their upkeep - I contribute towards things like clothes and other bits they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's useful information.

**How much do you currently contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month? I need to know this so I can compare it to the Child Benefit payment amount to see if your contributions meet the threshold.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £20 a week towards Alex's needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. That's helpful.

**How long has Alex been living with someone else rather than with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been living with their other parent for quite a while now - it's been the arrangement for some time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify a couple more details to complete the assessment.

**Is the other parent (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know.

**When exactly did Alex move to live with the other parent? I need to know the specific date or approximate timeframe (for example, how many weeks or months ago) so I can determine if you're still within the eligibility period.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been quite a long time now - Alex has been living there for over a year, maybe closer to two years actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's important information.

I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me work through the rules:

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes to live with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for **8 weeks** after they move, if nobody else is claiming. However, you can continue to get payments for **longer than 8 weeks if you make contributions to your child's upkeep** that are at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment.

In your case:
- Alex has been living with the other parent for over a year (well beyond the initial 8 weeks)
- You are contributing £20 per week towards Alex's needs
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The current Child Benefit rate is £24.50 per week for the first child. Your contribution of £20 per week is **less than** the Child Benefit payment amount of £24.50 per week.

According to the rules, your contributions need to be at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment for you to continue claiming beyond the initial 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Here's why:
- Since Alex has been living with the other parent for over a year, you're outside the initial 8-week grace period
- To continue claiming beyond 8 weeks, your contributions towards Alex's upkeep must be **at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount** (currently £24.50 per week)
- Your contributions of £20 per week are below this threshold

**What you could do:**
If you were able to increase your contributions to at least £24.50 per week (or £106 per month), you would then meet the eligibility criteria. You would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to report this change in circumstances.

If you have any questions or if your circumstances change, I'd recommend contacting HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Child Benefit Office for further advice.
